component.name: crumBS
component.summary: Find and remove app leftovers, caches and system bloat

description.p: crumBS lists the apps installed from your package manager, Flatpak, Snap and AppImages, and finds what each one leaves behind: configuration, caches, data and system files. It removes an app together with its leftovers after showing you exactly what will go, and it cleans caches, logs, trash and orphan packages.
Every deletion is previewed, checked against safety rules, recorded and can be restored. crumBS also serves its tools to AI assistants over MCP.
System leftovers no longer offer software in /opt that is still linked, on your PATH or running. An installed snap's data is matched to it. uQ's Storage page says why a Put back found nothing.

uQ's Storage and cleanup page redesigned: apps sorted by category with an Uninstall button inside each app's own tile, and the same tiles for cleanups, leftovers and history. Apps carry a category in the JSON.
New uninstall --close-running, used by uQ's Storage and cleanup page to close an open app (CopyQ, say) before removing it. Sizes on compressed btrfs are marked, and fewer false orphans.
On the uQ desktop: a rebuilt Storage and cleanup page with tabs, app icons, progress, a preview of everything an uninstall removes, system leftovers and crumBS's settings. New crumbs config command.
On the uQ desktop: a Storage and cleanup page in Settings and an "Uninstall…" entry in the app menus. New uninstall --desktop-id.
Reaches further: project build folders, container images, pamac build trees, Electron app caches, uninstalled packages in the package cache and old Timeshift snapshots.
Works with the uQ desktop: guards its packages and leaves appOFholding's AppImages alone. Safer cache cleaning, signed releases.
